title: Minimum Moves to Capture The Queen
summary: Given a 1-indexed 8x8 chessboard with a white rook, a white bishop, and a black queen, determine the minimum moves needed to capture the queen using only the rook and bishop.
statement: Given a 1-indexed 8x8 chessboard with a white rook, a white bishop, and a black queen, determine the minimum moves needed to capture the queen using only the rook and bishop. Rooks can move vertically or horizontally any number of squares, while bishops can move diagonally any number of squares. Neither can jump over pieces. The queen remains stationary.
constraints: All coordinates are from one through eight, with rook at (a,b), bishop at (c,d), queen at (e,f), and no shared square.
A rook attacks along rows and columns; a bishop attacks along diagonals; neither may jump over the other white piece.
Return one if either has a clear direct attack, otherwise two.
reference_solution:
def minimum_queen_capture_moves(a,b,c,d,e,f):
    rook_clear_row=a==e and not (c==a and min(b,f)<d<max(b,f))
    rook_clear_column=b==f and not (d==b and min(a,e)<c<max(a,e))
    bishop_aligned=abs(c-e)==abs(d-f)
    bishop_blocked=abs(a-e)==abs(b-f) and abs(a-c)==abs(b-d) and min(c,e)<a<max(c,e)
    return 1 if rook_clear_row or rook_clear_column or (bishop_aligned and not bishop_blocked) else 2

hints: Only a direct attack can finish in one move; otherwise the unobstructed board always permits capture in two.
Test rook row/column alignment and bishop diagonal alignment, excluding cases where the other piece lies strictly between attacker and queen.
Evaluate the two rook rays and four bishop rays with blocker checks; return one on any clear ray, else two.
The ray tests exactly characterize legal one-move captures, and when none exists a white piece can reposition to create a capture on its following move.

tests.explanation: Neither white piece attacks the queen initially, so repositioning and then capturing needs two moves.
The rook shares row five with the queen and the bishop does not block the adjacent path, so one move suffices.
